body:
So if this is only for API docs then it is the responsibility of `typescript` dgeni-package, since we do not use `readFilesProcessor` for acquiring TypeScript files - the TS compiler does that for us.

Except for generating links to stuff on github, I think that the OS ensures that the symlinks provide us with the correct content when we ask for it. It is a shame that github is not clever enough to do rewrites for us to match the the OS.

I guess the safest thing (to prevent unexpected BCs) would be to add an extra property to the `FileInfo` class (something like `realFilePath` or similar) which we can use for the github links.

issue.title: feat(typescript): add `realFilePath`/`realProjectRelativePath` to `FileInfo`

repository.name: dgeni-packages
repository.description: A collection of dgeni packages for generating documentation from source code.

issue.body:
The file paths returned by TypeScript may contain symlinks. This is fine most of the time, since the path points to the correct file, but in certain cases (e.g. when we want to generate GitHub links based on the project-relative path) it is necessary to know the real path to the file (without symlinks).

This commit adds two new properties, `realFilePath` and `realProjectRelativePath`, which are based on the real path to the file.

(Related to angular/angular#18353.)

issue.title: fix(aio): fix links to source for paths with symlinks
